title: Detection by the open and the closed restriction
statement: Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion, with complementary quasi-compact open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$. Let $R_X$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, and use the identified inverse-image coefficient sheaves and module operations of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. If an $R_X$-module sheaf $F$ has zero inverse images $j^*F=0$ and $i^*F=0$, then $F=0$.

proof.text: Write $R_Z=i^{-1}R_X$ and $R_U=j^{-1}R_X$. First transport the given coefficient identifications back to these rings. By [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], for an inverse-image coefficient isomorphism $c:u^{-1}R_X\xrightarrow{\sim}R_T$, the map $m\otimes r\mapsto c^{-1}(r)m$ identifies $u^*F$ with $u^{-1}F$, with its action transported along $c$; its inverse is $m\mapsto m\otimes1$. Thus $i^*F=0$ and $j^*F=0$ imply that the modules $i^{-1}F$ over $R_Z$ and $j^{-1}F$ over $R_U$ are zero. In particular no constancy or finiteness of $R_X$ is required.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] with $A=R_X$ and $M=F$. Its hypotheses are precisely a scheme $X$, a closed immersion $i$, and its complementary quasi-compact open immersion $j$. The coefficient rings there are $i^{-1}R_X$ and $j^{-1}R_X$, as in step 1. Its short exact sequence, with the actual counit and unit maps, is $0\to j_!j^{-1}F\to F\to i_*i^{-1}F\to0$. Only this sequence and the stated adjunction $j_!\dashv j^{-1}$ are used; the node's filtered-colimit clause and its extra qcqs hypothesis are not used.

proof.text: The two end terms in the short exact sequence are zero. Indeed, the direct-image formula of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] evaluates $i_*0$ at each object $W$ as $0(Z\times_XW)=0$. For $j_!0$, the adjunction in [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] gives $\operatorname{Hom}(j_!0,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(0,j^{-1}N)$, a singleton for every $N$; hence $j_!0$ is initial and is the zero module sheaf. Exactness at $F$, in [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence], now equates the image of $0\to F$ with the kernel of $F\to0$. These are respectively the zero subobject and the whole object $F$. Therefore $F$ is the zero module sheaf, as claimed.
